item.title: India IPO Hopefuls Race to Beat August Deadline for Audited Results
item.description: Three offerings closed on Monday, while four more firms have announced IPO schedules.

item.title: Origin Says About 900,000 Customers’ Data Accessed in Breach
item.description: About 900,000 current and former Origin Energy Ltd. customers had their data accessed in a security breach, the latest in a string of cyberattacks on major Australian companies and essential-service providers.

item.title: Innolight Prices $6.8 Billion Hong Kong Listing Below Maximum
item.description: Zhongji Innolight Co. raised HK$53.4 billion ($6.8 billion) after pricing its Hong Kong listing below the maximum offered in one of the city’s biggest first-time share sale in seven years.

item.title: Anthropic’s Amodei Rejects Open Model Ban But Calls for Testing
item.description: Silicon Valley leaders, including Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei and Nvidia Corp. CEO Jensen Huang, are warning against a broad government crackdown on open-weight artificial intelligence systems as a response to a breakthrough Chinese AI model that’s challenged US leadership in the technology.

item.title: Koei Tecmo Shares Fall as Earnings Miss, Long-Term Doubts Grow
item.description: Shares of Koei Tecmo Holdings Co. fell the most since March after the video-game publisher reported first-quarter operating profit that missed market expectations, underscoring weak software sales and fueling investor concerns about its long-term growth prospects.

item.title: Takaichi’s Long-Term Vision May Fail to Dispel Inflation Angst
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s long-term vision for powering the nation’s growth through domestic investment risks becoming a hollow ambition if she fails to address shorter-term angst over the cost of living.

item.title: Takaichi’s Looming Tax Cut Plan Risks Weighing on Yen, JGBs
item.description: A looming announcement from Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi to go ahead with a plan to cut Japan’s sales tax on food risks pressuring the yen and government bonds by stoking investor concerns over the country’s deteriorating fiscal outlook.

item.title: Japanese, Korean Stocks Tumble as Chip Selloff Intensifies
item.description: Japanese and South Korean stocks slid, led by semiconductor shares, as concerns over Nvidia Corp.’s blockbuster AI supply deal and intensifying competition from Chinese chipmakers weighed on investor sentiment.

item.title: Japan’s Takaichi to Order Food Tax Cut to 1%, Reports Say
item.description: The Japanese government plans to cut the sales tax on food and drinks to 1% for two years starting next April, according to local media reports, delivering one of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s signature election pledges after months of political wrangling.

item.title: Chip Rout Deepens on Circular Funding, China Competition Fears
item.description: A selloff in global semiconductor stocks deepened on Tuesday, as investor sentiment continued to worsen over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: CXMT Listing Creates $192 Billion Windfall for Chinese Province
item.description: A Chinese province better known globally for its stunning mountain landscapes than its technology investments has this week joined the ranks of the biggest winners from the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Australia’s ‘World-First’ Data Center Rules Face First Hurdle
item.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese’s proposed “world-first” environmental and energy controls for Australia’s A$150 billion ($105 billion) data center pipeline will face their first test Tuesday, when federal, state and territory energy ministers meet to discuss guardrails for the booming sector.

item.title: SK Hynix’s $570 Billion Selloff Shows Cracks in Memory-Chip Boom
item.description: A $570 billion rout in just a little over a month has flipped SK Hynix Inc. from one of the world’s hottest AI trades to one of the biggest portfolio question marks.

item.title: Gold Declines as Traders Weigh Prospects for Interest-Rate Hike
item.description: Gold declined ahead of a potentially divisive decision on US interest rates later this week, while a fragile pause in Middle East hostilities soothed inflation fears.

item.title: UK Food Inflation Falls for Sixth Consecutive Month, BRC Says
item.description: UK food inflation has fallen for a sixth straight month, a retail trade association said Tuesday, after shops discounted snacks and alcohol to entice millions of fans watching England reach the semi-finals of the World Cup.

item.title: Oil Extends Decline, Asian Stocks Set for Losses: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian equities are set for a mostly weaker open after a selloff in chipmakers dragged US stocks lower, even as oil extended losses.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for July 28
item.description: Oil extended a steep drop after President Donald Trump said the US and Iran were engaged in talks to end the Middle East conflict.

item.title: BlackRock Raises $12.5 Billion of Debt for Meta Data Center
item.description: BlackRock Inc. wrapped up a $12.5 billion bond sale tied to a Meta Platforms Inc. data center project in Texas after a nearly week-long marketing process and a selloff in big tech debt.

item.title: Citadel Securities Sees Warsh Delivering Surprise Fed Rate Hike
item.description: Citadel Securities expects the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates this week — a surprise move strengthening Chairman Kevin Warsh’s credibility in the battle with inflation.

item.title: Curium Is Said to Near About $7 Billion Acquisition of Lantheus
item.description: Curium is in advanced talks to acquire radiopharma company Lantheus Holdings Inc. in a deal that could be announced in the coming days, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: CME’s Debut of 24/7 Gold Futures Trading Met With Strong Demand
item.description: CME Group Inc. said the debut weekend of 24/7 trading for its one-ounce gold futures saw stronger-than-expected demand with deep liquidity despite subdued volatility.

item.title: S. Korea’s Consumer Confidence Hits Four-Month High on Chip Boom
item.description: South Korea’s consumer confidence climbed for a third straight month in July as an artificial intelligence-driven semiconductor boom and expectations for stronger wage growth offset concerns over elevated inflation and recent stock-market losses.

item.title: BlackRock Dodges AI Bond Flop as $12.3 Billion Debt Deal Rallies
item.description: Bonds that BlackRock Inc. is selling, tied to a Meta Platforms Inc. data center project in Texas, rallied in early trading on Monday before the notes were formally priced, signaling demand for the securities may be stronger than it initially appeared.

item.title: SK Hynix Slumps Below US IPO Price as Mega-Listings Turn Sour
item.description: SK Hynix Inc.’s American depositary receipts slumped to a new low after a record-setting $26.5 billion debut earlier this month as investors dump once-high flying semiconductor stocks.

item.title: Lenders to Distressed Cloud Tech Firm Dye & Durham Tap Advisers
item.description: Dye & Durham Ltd.’s lenders have retained Houlihan Lokey Inc. as financial adviser as the software company’s capital position comes under increased scrutiny, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: XP Founder Urges Brazil to Fix Deficit as Election Debate Looms
item.description: Guilherme Benchimol, the founder and chairman of brokerage firm XP Inc., has a warning: A meaningful fiscal overhaul is essential if the country is to bring interest rates down and create a better environment for investing.

item.title: Azimut Fund Manager Bets on Japanese Bonds as Yields Surge
item.description: Japanese government bonds offer investors one of the best opportunities in global fixed income despite being viewed as high risk, according to an Azimut Group fund manager.

item.title: Trump Latest Tariffs on 60 Economies Face New Legal Challenges: Big Take Podcast
item.description: Economists agree the Section 301 tariffs are designed to hold up under scrutiny.

item.title: Angola Raises $321 Million Through Nation’s Biggest IPO
item.description: Angola has raised 300.3 billion kwanzas ($321 million) through the sale of 15% stake in state-owned wireless operator Unitel SA, marking the southwest African nation’s biggest initial public offering.

item.title: Orange, Morrison Partner on French Data Center Project
item.description: Orange SA and infrastructure manager Morrison are joining forces to create a data center company in France in an effort to strengthen Europe’s digital sovereignty.
